question: what is stopping us from courting more names?
answer: Court throughput is NOT the binding constraint, and treating it as one has been the error. The arithmetic: today's six new positions averaged $16.5k. Deployable capital after the tax reserve is ~$3.3M. That is 200 POSITIONS, or ~1,000 courts at today's 2-clear-per-10 rate — 40 more days as heavy as the heaviest court day on record. No process of this depth can produce that, and no book can hold 200 researched names.
the_real_constraint: POSITION SIZE. Every court this session sized 0.27-0.50% of the eventual ~$4.4M book, against a doctrine that allows ~1.2% (OMF was ruled 1.17% = $70k). We are sizing at roughly HALF the ruled cap on names that cleared BOTH a court and a mandatory red team — ISRG 6/10 got $18.9k, DSGX 6/10 got $22.1k.
the_implication: a 40-60 name book is the most a process of this depth can carry, and $3.3M across 50 names is ~$66k each — 4x today's average size. Either sizes rise on the highest-conviction verdicts, or the deployment target is wrong and a large part of the $5M should never be single-name equity at all.

the_three_mechanical_blockers_and_their_.weight: REAL but transient — resets next session; it is why tonight's courts ran inline, which is a weaker check (I flagged it on Cleanup and the ADIG price basis)
REAL but routable — EDGAR via curl and WebFetch closed every decisive question tonight (BSX's cause, ADIG's information statement, the Parametric extracts)
REAL and specific — the AI-adopter 80 need per-name segment revenue + labour series before ANY of them can be courted; that is research, not adjudication

what_this_does_NOT_mean: it is not an argument to lower the bar. The blue teams tested that today: 3 of 3 rejections moved on instrumentation, 0 of 3 flipped on conviction. The bar is calibrated. The problem is that a calibrated bar producing 2 clears per 10 courts, at 0.4% per clear, cannot deploy the capital in any reasonable time.
the_decision_owed_to_the_principal: Option A — SIZE UP the high-conviction verdicts. A 6/10 that survived a mandatory red team is the highest-quality signal this process produces; sizing it at 0.43% wastes the work. Moving 6/10-plus names to 1.0-1.5% would deploy ~$3.3M across ~50-60 names, which is a carryable book.
Option B — accept a MULTI-YEAR deployment horizon and hold the residual in SGOV at ~2.55% after tax. Coherent, and the tax reserve already forces part of it.

Option C — split the mandate: the court book takes what it can carry at honest size (~$1.5-2M across 40-50 names) and the residual goes to a tax-managed index sleeve that harvests. This is the barbell I recommended for the Parametric question and it applies identically here.
NOT an option — courting 200 names. The process cannot do it and the book cannot hold it.
my_recommendation: A and C together: raise sizing on red-team-survivors to ~1.0-1.5%, cap the court book at ~50 names, and route the residual to a harvesting sleeve rather than letting it sit in SGOV earning 2.55% after tax while the loss bank we need for 2027 goes unbuilt.
